excluded: RTT/Karn, delayed ACK, complete persist, congestion/recovery
RST challenge validation, SYN/data and urgent/options handling
multiple connections and half-space ambiguous inputs
independent implementation evidence and universal content/output proofs

FIN-SPACE.interpretation: SEG.LEN includes FIN control octet after all payload. A FIN marker is separate from the byte buffer and is acknowledged exactly once.

FIN-QUEUE.interpretation: Queue acceptable ahead FIN until all preceding bytes become contiguous; drain text and FIN before one cumulative ACK (Table 6, MUST-59). FIN outside the offered receive interval is trimmed and must be retransmitted.

FIN-WINDOW.interpretation: Explicit FIN-segment headers use existing sequence-before-ACK and WL1/WL2 window processing before text/FIN; unacceptable sequence or future ACK cannot consume or install FIN.

FIN-CLOSE.interpretation: After contiguous FIN consumption enter CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING or TIME-WAIT as appropriate, including own FIN acknowledged in the same segment; duplicate FIN cannot deliver EOF twice and restarts TIME-WAIT only at the already consumed FIN position.

FIN-SCOPE.interpretation: Single shared 16-byte receive queue and one FIN marker. First accepted marker wins for contradictory FIN positions; queued bytes at/after that EOF are discarded. Legacy net.fin has no observed window/payload; net.fin_segment is the complete declared FIN header event.
